At the time of his [[National Letter of Intent]] signing with [[Michigan Wolverines basketball]], [[ESPN.com]] and [[Scout.com]] ranked McGary as the number two player in the United States high school class of 2012, while [[Rivals.com]] ranked him as the number three prospect. He was not only the consensus top [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] recruit in the nation,{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/touted-hoops-recruit-mcgary-commits-michigan|title=Touted hoops recruit Mitch McGary commits to Michigan|accessdate=2011-11-18|date=2011-11-03|publisher=[[Michigan Daily]]|author=Estes, Ben}} but also the top [[Glossary of basketball terms#B|big man]] according to most sources at the time.{{cite web|url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/campusrivalry/post/2011/11/top-big-man-recruit-mitch-mcgary-commits-to-michigan/1|title=Nation's No. 2 basketball recruit Mitch McGary commits to Michigan|accessdate=2011-12-31|date=2011-11-03|work=[[USA Today]]}} After his signing, however, McGary fell down in the rankings as his underdeveloped offensive skills became apparent. At Michigan, McGary became the [[sixth man]] as well as the leading [[blocked shot|shot blocker]] and [[rebound (basketball)|rebounder]] for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team]]. During the season, he was twice named Big Ten Freshman of the Week. He became the regular starter during the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/mcgary-robinson-will-return-2013-14-season|title=McGary, Robinson will return for 2013-14 season|accessdate=2013-04-18|date=2013-04-18|work=[[Michigan Daily]]|author=Thomas, Colleen}} and earned South All-Regional Team and NCAA All-Tournament Team recognition. He led all Big Ten Freshman in rebounding. ==Background== [[File:20110110 Mitch McGary at Hoop Hall Classic.jpg|thumb|left|McGary at [[Brewster Academy|Brewster]]]] Mitch McGary was born on June 6, 1992,{{cite web|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/669yfQCG2|archivedate=2012-03-14|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/hoopsummit/roster.html|title=Nike Hoop Summit - USA & World Team Rosters|accessdate=2012-03-14|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}} and grew up in the [[Chesterton, Indiana]], area. He played in [[YMCA]] and [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball leagues as a youth, and his father, Tim, who had never played organized sports, coached him until fourth grade.{{cite web|url=http://www.dukehoopblog.com/2011/10/12/through-the-eyes-of-a-father-mitch-mcgary/|title=Through the Eyes of a Father: Mitch McGary|accessdate=2011-11-18|date=2011-10-12|work=Duke Hoop Blog}} McGary's mother is named Valerie.{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/mitch-mcgary-you-dont-know-through-eyes-his-parents|title=The Mitch McGary you don't know, through the eyes of his parents|accessdate=2013-03-31|date=2012-11-08|work=Michigan Daily|author=Wasserman, Daniel}} When McGary was younger, his father thought his athletic future was in [[baseball]]. McGary played on the 2007–08 [[Chesterton High School]] [[junior varsity team]] as a freshman, while eventual three-time [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] [[captain (sports)|captain]] Zack Novak was a senior on the [[varsity team]]. That year he also was a {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|2|adj=on}}, {{convert|190|lbs|kg|0|adj=on}} freshman [[tight end]] on the [[high school football]] team, but his father made him quit football as he continued to grow.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/81287/mcgary-offers-a-new-dimension-for-michigan|title=McGary offers new dimension for Michigan|accessdate=2013-03-24|date=2013-03-23|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}} His local Indiana SPY Players AAU basketball team included future Michigan teammates Max Bielfeldt and [[Glenn Robinson III]], son of [[Glenn Robinson]]. McGary joined the varsity basketball team the following season and played two years. McGary is afflicted with [[attention deficit hyperactivity disorder]]. He eventually transferred to [[Brewster Academy]], a prep school in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], to repeat his junior year because his parents thought the discipline would be good for him. Before transferring to Brewster, McGary was the tallest kid in his school and in the basketball conference that he played in.
